thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty P24680 fired for service=redwood-inference-gpu-hosts \u2014 symptom: kubelet CrashLoop/NodeNotReady on host gpu-node-42 \u2014 severity: P1 \u2014 link: https://pd.redwood/p/P24680

pagerduty-bot: P24680 -> Acknowledged by ben (on-call). Escalation timer started (4m).

ben: ack. I'm taking lead. Lina please grab kernel logs and console output, Otto monitor exporters/metrics.

lina: pulling logs from serial console. dmesg shows a hard kernel panic referencing "BUG: unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at 00000000deadbeef" and stacktrace in module drivers/gpu/nv/abc.c. kernel log truncated; serial shows "Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception" around 03:12:09Z.

otto: prometheus: node_exporter for gpu-node-42 went down at 03:12, nvml-exporter timed out. Grafana: inference-hosted latency spiked +5% and API 502s in us-west-2.

ben: can we ssh? try now. If serial is the only console, we may need a power-cycle.

rory: ssh attempts hang; TCP connection establishes then stalls at auth. IPMI shows host responsive but kernel panic happened before network stack recovered. We can pull serial logs — Lina are you copying to S3?

lina: copying serial log now: `aws s3 cp /var/log/serial/gpu-node-42/2026-03-29-03:12.log s3://redwood-incident-logs/P24680/` -> done. I'll paste the last 40 lines below for quick triage:
```
[  181.234567] BUG: unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at 00000000deadbeef
[  181.234578] RIP: 0010:gpu_driver_fault+0x4f/0x120 [nv_driver]
[  181.234590] Code: Bad RIP value.
[  181.234600] ---[ end trace 9f12c3d4 ]---
[  181.234610] Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception
```

ops-support: customer-facing note request: what services impacted? I see retries on inference-hosted pods that were pinned to that host.

ben: partial impact to hosted inference in us-west-2; customers seeing transient 5xxs. Ops-support please draft status update stating partial degraded performance in region and we're investigating host-level failure.

pagerduty-bot: P24680 escalation: 2m until next level.

otto: check if we can migrate pods: node is in kernel panic and not responding to kubelet, so cordon/drain won't work until host recovers. We should prepare failover for pods on other nodes.

ben: Agreed. Trigger failover by marking node unschedulable in k8s once API accepts it; but first attempt soft recovery. Lina, any chance to trigger sysrq to sync and remount ro to flush logs?

lina: IPMI supports serial-over-lan but remote sysrq commands not exposed without root on host. Since kernel panic already happened, soft remediation unlikely. Recommend power-cycle via BMC.

rory: initiating BMC power-cycle now: `ipmitool -I lanplus -H bmc-gpu-42 -U admin -P **** chassis power cycle` -> command sent. Host should come back within ~90s.

ben: notify infra on-call about potential side effects. Sara take post-reboot monitoring.

sara: ack. monitoring dashboards on watch.

rory: host is powering up. I see PXE/boot messages on serial.

otto: while it boots, I'll prepare a node eviction plan and cordon once kubelet registers. Also prepare to recreate pods pinned to local-ephemeral volumes.

rory: host booted, but kubelet enters CrashLoopBackOff on start: `kubelet: failed to start: failed to create kubelet server: error creating proxier: conntrack table full` per journal. conntrack shows table at max entries (nf_conntrack_count=65536).

ben: that's different. conntrack full can block kube-proxy and kubelet proxy components. Otto can you clear conntrack and tune?

otto: running `conntrack -S` -> shows high number of tcp entries in TIME_WAIT and ESTABLISHED from a burst of pod migrations earlier. Clearing with `conntrack -F` will remove state and may briefly disrupt active connections. Given degraded state, proceeding.

otto: `sudo conntrack -F` executed. Kernel nf_conntrack_count dropped to 120. Restarting kubelet and kube-proxy: `sudo systemctl restart kube-proxy kubelet`.

lina: kubelet comes up cleanly now. `kubectl get nodes` shows gpu-node-42 Ready. NV drivers load fine; `nvidia-smi` reports all GPUs OK.

ben: uncordon or keep cordoned while we let scheduler rebalance?

otto: leave cordoned for 10m to ensure no immediate pod placement onto node until metrics stable. I'll also add a temporary nodeSelector to avoid scheduling heavy inference pods for a brief window.

ops-support: status page: posted update "Partial degradation resolved; host rebooted and node recovered; remediation in progress. Follow-up postmortem to follow."

pagerduty-bot: P24680 -> Resolved by ben at 2026-03-29T03:21:28Z. Summary: kernel panic in GPU driver caused host-level kernel panic, node became NotReady. BMC power-cycle recovered host; kernel recovered but kubelet initially blocked by conntrack exhaustion -> cleared state and restarted services. Logs uploaded to s3://redwood-incident-logs/P24680/; dmesg and serial logs saved.

lina: creating postmortem ticket with dmesg, nv driver version, conntrack stats, and action items: 1) enable persistent serial logging to central S3 for all GPU hosts; 2) add alert for nf_conntrack nearing threshold and tune kubelet/kube-proxy conntrack debit; 3) add runbook for BMC power-cycle and preferred order of operations (avoid touching container runtime unless necessary); 4) evaluate kernel driver regression and coordinate vendor driver update.

ben: thanks team. Handing off to sara for 2h of watch. Sara please escalate to infra if any kernel oops repeats.

sara: ack and watching graphs.

ben: closing thread in 30m if stable. :white_check_mark:
